substantive_reconstruction.full_gram: The first p columns of U=[B,F;G,H] have Gram B†B+G†G=I. Thus ||Bx||^2=||x||^2-||Gx||^2 for EVERY x, proving contraction. The original individual-column inference is indeed insufficient: columns of[1,1;0,0] have length1 but the normalized vector(1,1)/sqrt2 is sent to(sqrt2,0). The candidate corrects that implication, not the true unitary-compression theorem.
substantive_reconstruction.rotated_columns: B=W1 C V1† gives (GV1)†GV1=I-C^2, whose diagonal entries are nonnegative and off-diagonal entries zero. Thus0<=c_j<=1 and the lower columns have orthogonal lengths s_j=sqrt(1-c_j^2). Nonzero s_j can be divided out. At s_j=0 the column vanishes and one chooses an orthonormal complement vector instead; q>=p guarantees enough dimensions. Repeated c_j impose no uniqueness requirement.
substantive_reconstruction.complete_factorization: After left diag(W1†,W2†) and right diag(V1,I), the first columns are L=[C;S;0]. For K=[[S,0],[-C,0],[0,I]], direct multiplication gives L†L=I,K†K=I,L†K=0. There are p+q columns in[L,K], so it is unitary. The remaining transformed columns Y span the same orthogonal complement, hence K†Y is a q-dimensional unitary; naming it V2† gives Y=K V2† and exactly the advertised signed CS factorization. q=p removes the third block; p=0 reduces to an arbitrary remaining unitary. No QR uniqueness or invertible S is assumed.

General nonnormal eigenvalues are not SVT arguments and a target encoded at scale alpha supplies sigma(A)/alpha. The real-angle formulas are valid in this interval, with second-kind polynomial endpoints±(l+1) as specified.
